answer: Each identity drills one core on a mesa rim above a canyon, seals it with an umber stamp binding it to its key, and locks a 70-credit bond. The first core costs 33; the k-th core on the same funding key costs 33+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6027 and 1000 fake cores cost 3,030,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. An auditor re-adds strata thicknesses from the drill log against the depth; a mismatch, a reused core, or one key holding two cores burns the bond. A rented-core ring fails: the rented core carries the lender key, not the borrower key. An honest driller pays 33 once and keeps the bond.
